Product case study · Public summary

Trend-based advertising beyond the search box

How can a retail platform recognize when a cultural or social trend signals genuine shopping intent, then connect the right customers with relevant products and messages?

My contributionProduct framing and narrative, PRFAQ and requirements, signal-to-discovery workflow, and an experimentation approach for incremental value.

Why this problem matters

Search remains an important expression of intent, but it starts after a customer knows what to ask for. A trend can shape interest earlier: someone encounters a style, activity, creator, or cultural moment and begins exploring what to buy.

I framed a product hypothesis around that earlier moment, particularly for Gen Z and other emerging audiences whose discovery journeys may begin outside conventional search. Timely inspiration may lead to more spontaneous purchases, but attention alone does not prove buying intent. The opportunity was to distinguish commerce-driven trends from general conversation, then help customers move from inspiration to a useful retail decision.

In the Amazon context, I considered how trend-aware discovery could connect customers to the broader retail and Prime value proposition of selection, price, and convenience. That connection had to be earned through relevant products and a good shopping experience.

“Can we turn a trend into relevant discovery without treating every spike in attention as purchase intent?”

The product approach

I developed the what-and-why narrative, a PRFAQ-style proposal, and product requirements, then worked through an executed project that converted aggregated trend signals into a discovery and advertising workflow. The public description below captures the decision logic at a conceptual level.

01 / Understand

Aggregate and classify trend signals

Combine signals across multiple sources, identify trend type, market, and audience context, and distinguish shopping-relevant momentum from broad attention.

02 / Match

Translate interest into retail relevance

Use the trend interpretation to guide retrieval, ranking, filtering, product and creative selection, customer messaging, and which audiences should see the experience.

03 / Learn

Measure what was incremental

Use controlled experiments and an automated view of how response changes with trend strength, segment, and timing.

Classifying the shape of a trend

Different trends need different treatment. A short-lived local spike should not be handled like a broad, sustained shift. We classified signals into trend types and interpreted them at the marketplace level across a worldwide stores business.

Micro trends

Focused, often fast-moving pockets of attention whose relevance may be limited to a particular audience or moment.

Macro trends

Broader changes that persist across more customers, products, or time.

Theme trends

Related interests that form a coherent topic even when customers describe it in different ways.

Festival and event trends

Interest shaped by a specific occasion, with timing and local context central to relevance.

The same theme can mean different things in different marketplaces. The model therefore had to account for local demand, language, selection, and timing before treating a trend as a commerce opportunity.

PRFAQ, in brief

Public reconstruction of the product narrative

Press release concept

Customers can discover products connected to emerging interests at the moment those interests become relevant to them. A trend-aware experience identifies shopping-oriented trends, finds suitable selection, and presents useful messages and creative in context.

Who is the customer?

A shopper whose interest is sparked by a trend and who has not yet formed a precise search query. The advertiser and retail teams also need confidence that the experience reaches relevant audiences and creates incremental value.

Why would the customer trust it?

The recommendation should fit the trend and the person, lead to appropriate products, and preserve the retail fundamentals of selection, price, and convenience. Attention alone is not sufficient reason to advertise.

How would we know it works?

Compare exposed and control groups, examine downstream shopping actions, and test whether value is truly incremental rather than merely shifting demand that would have occurred anyway.

Requirements that shaped the work

The core product requirement was to make trend detection actionable while maintaining relevance and measurement discipline. A trend should enter the advertising workflow only when there is credible commercial context and suitable selection.

Customers also describe interests in multiple languages across search surfaces. We reused lessons from our query-understanding and classification work to interpret those expressions and improve semantic matching between a trend, the customer's query, and relevant products. That made ranking more sensitive to language and marketplace context without requiring a public claim about a specific ranking-score lift.

Trend understanding

Group related signals, recognize changes over time, and distinguish commerce-driven themes from general cultural discussion.

Market and language context

Interpret a theme at the marketplace level and recognize how customers express related intent in different languages.

Segment awareness

Understand which customer groups and contexts are responding, rather than assuming a trend has the same meaning for everyone.

Discovery relevance

Retrieve and rank products that genuinely fit the theme; filter out weak or unsuitable matches.

Creative and message fit

Align the product, creative, and message with the underlying customer interest and buying moment.

Retail quality

Respect selection, price, and convenience so the trend experience strengthens the broader shopping journey.

Measurement

Instrument outcomes by trend type and segment, with controls that separate incremental behavior from correlated activity.

Experimentation and elasticity

The measurement question was not simply whether a trend attracted clicks. It was whether the experience brought the right customers to relevant selection and produced additional shopping value.

Incrementality

Use test and control comparisons to assess whether trend-aware discovery changes meaningful shopping outcomes beyond what existing channels would have delivered.

Trend response

Track how performance changes as a trend grows, peaks, and fades; compare response across trend types, customer segments, and product groups. This creates an automated view of where trend intensity translates into commerce.

This public case study describes product thinking and the categories of work completed. It does not publish internal data sources, implementation details, experiment results, or numeric business outcomes. I can discuss my role and decision process in more detail in a conversation.
